description: Dense recurrent collateral synapses among CA3 pyramidal neurons, strengthened by NMDAR-dependent Hebbian plasticity, store memory patterns as distributed attractor states. When a partial cue arrives via perforant path or mossy fiber input, recurrent excitation among CA3 pyramidals iteratively fills in missing activity, converging on the stored attractor; feedback inhibition keeps activity sparse and stable. The completed CA3 pattern is then read out by CA1, supporting recall from degraded cues as demonstrated by Nakazawa et al.'s CA3-NR1 knockout.
